theory.intro: Most figures need more than one rule. Work one angle at a time, using whichever triangle, quadrilateral or polygon property fits. The interior and exterior angles of polygons often give you the first fact.
facts: In a triangle the angle sum is $180^{\circ}$, and an exterior angle equals the sum of the two interior opposite angles.
The base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal, and every angle of an equilateral triangle is $60^{\circ}$.
In a quadrilateral the angle sum is $360^{\circ}$, opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal, and every angle of a rectangle or square is $90^{\circ}$.
In a regular $n$-gon each interior angle is $\frac{180(n-2)}{n}$ and each exterior angle is $\frac{360}{n}$.
A diagonal joining vertices on either side of one vertex of a regular polygon forms an isosceles triangle with the two intervening sides.
Angles on a straight line add to $180^{\circ}$, angles at a point add to $360^{\circ}$, and vertically opposite angles are equal.
On parallel lines, alternate angles are equal and co-interior angles add to $180^{\circ}$.
Write a reason after every line: a value with no reason is not a finished answer.
The interior angle sum of an $n$-sided polygon is $180(n-2)^{\circ}$. The exterior angles of a convex polygon, one at each vertex, add to $360^{\circ}$.
steps: Mark every angle you can find, each with a reason.
Use a triangle, quadrilateral or polygon in which only one thing is unknown.
Repeat until you reach the required angle.

workedExamples.question_text: A regular pentagon and a regular octagon lie outside each other and share one complete side. Find the angle in the gap between their other sides at an endpoint of the shared side.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$I_5=180(5-2)^{\circ}\div5=108^{\circ}$ (interior angle of a regular pentagon)
$I_8=180(8-2)^{\circ}\div8=135^{\circ}$ (interior angle of a regular octagon)
$g+108^{\circ}+135^{\circ}=360^{\circ}$ (angles at a point)
$g=117^{\circ}$

workedExamples.solution_text:
$75^{\circ}+40^{\circ}+85^{\circ}+65^{\circ}+E=360^{\circ}$ (exterior angle sum)
$265^{\circ}+E=360^{\circ}$
$E=95^{\circ}$
$I+95^{\circ}=180^{\circ}$ (interior and exterior angles are supplementary)
$I=85^{\circ}$

workedExamples.question_text: The angles of a triangle are $(4a+10)^{\circ}$, $(3a+24)^{\circ}$ and $(4a-8)^{\circ}$. Show that the triangle is isosceles.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}(4a+10)+(3a+24)+(4a-8)&=180\\11a+26&=180\\11a&=154\\a&=14\end{aligned}$
Angles in a triangle sum to $180^{\circ}$.
$\begin{aligned}4a+10&=66\\3a+24&=66\\4a-8&=48\end{aligned}$
Two angles are $66^{\circ}$, so the triangle is isosceles.

workedExamples.question_text: The angles of a triangle are $(4a+12)^{\circ}$, $(3a+26)^{\circ}$ and $(4a-12)^{\circ}$. Show that the triangle is isosceles.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}(4a+12)+(3a+26)+(4a-12)&=180\\11a+26&=180\\11a&=154\\a&=14\end{aligned}$
Angles in a triangle sum to $180^{\circ}$.
$\begin{aligned}4a+12&=68\\3a+26&=68\\4a-12&=44\end{aligned}$
Two angles are $68^{\circ}$, so the triangle is isosceles.

workedExamples.question_text: In convex pentagon $ABCDE$, the interior angles at $B$, $C$ and $D$ are $90^{\circ}$, $145^{\circ}$ and $100^{\circ}$. Side $EA$ is extended beyond $A$, making an exterior angle of $60^{\circ}$ with $AB$. Find the interior angles at $A$ and $E$.

$S=180(5-2)^{\circ}=540^{\circ}$ (interior angle sum of a pentagon)

development.question_text: In convex pentagon $ABCDE$, the exterior angles at $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ are $78^{\circ}$, $42^{\circ}$, $105^{\circ}$ and $65^{\circ}$. Find the exterior angle $b$ and the interior angle $c$ at $E$.

$b=70^{\circ}$

development.question_text: In convex quadrilateral $ABCD$, the interior angle at $A$ is $90^{\circ}$. The exterior angles at $B$ and $C$ are $80^{\circ}$ and $125^{\circ}$. Find the exterior angle $d$ and interior angle $e$ at $D$.
development.solution_text:
$E_A=180^{\circ}-90^{\circ}=90^{\circ}$ (interior and exterior angles are supplementary)
$90^{\circ}+80^{\circ}+125^{\circ}+d=360^{\circ}$ (exterior angle sum)
$295^{\circ}+d=360^{\circ}$
$d=65^{\circ}$
$e=180^{\circ}-65^{\circ}=115^{\circ}$ (interior and exterior angles are supplementary)

mastery.question_text: The angles of a triangle are $(4a+20)^{\circ}$, $(3a+34)^{\circ}$ and $(4a-28)^{\circ}$. Show that the triangle is isosceles.
mastery.solution_text:
$(4a+20)+(3a+34)+(4a-28)=180$ (triangle angle sum)
$11a+26=180$
$11a=154$
$a=14$
$4a+20=76$
$3a+34=76$
$4a-28=28$
$\therefore$ two angles are $76^{\circ}$, so the triangle is isosceles.
